::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**The point of this page.** The target is a *published* simulation, so we know a
compact model exists — but we have only the paper, not the code. That makes it the
cleanest possible testbed for agentic mechanistic discovery: **if Plexus cannot
reconstruct a known model even with strong priors and a known answer, it will not
reconstruct an unknown one from real data, where the very existence of a model is in
doubt.** Success here is necessary, not sufficient; failure here would be decisive.
:::

## A controlled testbed

The target is Okuda *et&nbsp;al.* (2018): a Turing reaction–diffusion system discretised
at the single-cell level and coupled to a **3D vertex model**, which — by growing a
monolayer cell vesicle — reproduces autonomous *undulation*, *tubulation*, and
*branching*.[^okuda] We have the paper, and with it **strong priors**: a vertex-model
tissue, an activator–inhibitor reaction–diffusion, and growth converted from each cell's
activator concentration. We do **not** have the code. Reconstructing the result inside
[Plexus](index.qmd) is therefore a *blind* reproduction, driven by priors alone.

That is exactly what makes it the right problem to cut our teeth on. On real experimental
data the hardest uncertainty is not the parameters but whether a compact mechanistic model
*exists at all*. Here that question is settled — we know a model exists, and roughly what
it is — so this is the **easiest version of the real problem**, a controlled floor test for
the [three-loop agentic discovery](inverse.qmd) the project is built around. What is
interesting is precisely that the simulation is *blind* (no repository) yet the answer is
*known*: strong priors, a fixed target, and full freedom to run the forward model. If the
method works nowhere here, it works nowhere.

This page is the honest record of the attempt **so far** — a gallery of failures, because
the failures are where the method actually gets defined.

## The approach in brief

The reconstruction runs as the three loops described in the
[Plexus paper](paper/plexus2.pdf) (§&nbsp;*Agentic mechanistic discovery*):
**Understand** the target by interrogating a decomposed model — a hypothesis → *validate /
falsify* cycle held to a rough **70/30** balance; **Fit** its parameters and fields against
the differentiable operators; **Discover** the operators the model still lacks from the
residual. A **master** controller holds the goal, authors the success metrics, grounds each
hypothesis in Okuda's text, and — before trusting any measurement — enforces a *verify-the-
instrument* gate. Every stage is a small, metric-gated step, run cheap-first. The mechanical
substrate is the true-vertex [Tyssue](index.qmd#epithelial-mechanics-a-true-vertex-model)
tissue built elsewhere on this site; the morphogenesis is Okuda's coupling laid on top of it.

  buds the shell — but a <em>wide</em> activation grows the whole patch, folding a lobed

  that gap is the current front.</figcaption>

Behind these three lie the structural failures already crossed, each leaving a lesson that
is now part of the method:

- **Through-vertex division tangled** after one or two rounds → *edge-midpoint* division is
  the proliferation engine.
- **A single global lumen-volume term crumpled the shell** — one scalar constrains only the
  *sum* of cell volumes, so local dips are free → *distributed*, per-cell volume targets.
- **A "97% hollow" shell that no physics could fix** — because it was not physics: a
  recording-stride misalignment paired vertex positions with another frame's connectivity.
  *Verify the instrument before trusting the measurement.*
- **A synchronized division wave** (a grey band of exposed walls) — a deterministic cell
  cycle lock-steps under uniform growth → restore the biological noise of a *stochastic*
  cell cycle.
- **The reaction–diffusion choice is decisive** — the Brusselator decays or reorganizes the
  seed; only Gray–Scott (spot regime) and Gierer–Meinhardt hold a stable, localized peak.

## What the failures demand of the agent next

Read as a spec, the journey names the capabilities the autonomous master must carry — the
same [role spec](paper/plexus2.pdf) the paper argues for, now grounded in a real attempt:

- **Goal custody.** Several rounds drifted into locally-sensible sub-problems (homogenising a
  2000-cell sphere) and lost the tube; the master's objective must be held separately from
  the workers'.
- **Temporal perception.** The decisive evidence was in the *time course* — the grey band
  forms mid-growth, tip cells balloon early — invisible to an end-frame metric. A
  dynamics-watching critic is a required agent.
- **Verify the instrument.** The "97% hollow" shell and a false "0 invalid faces" (which
  passed self-intersecting bow-tie polygons) were diagnostic artefacts, not physics.
- **Literature grounding.** Reading *which* reaction–diffusion regime Okuda uses
  (Gierer–Meinhardt) was the single key unlock.
- **Domain priors and taste.** Reading the smooth activator *gradient* off Okuda's figures —
  rather than a binary switch — reframed the entire coupling.

The tube is not yet emergent. But every failure above has been converted from a symptom into
a measurable target, which is the whole point: this is what it looks like when a method, not
just a model, is being fit.

[^okuda]: Okuda, S., Miura, T., Inoue, Y., Adachi, T. & Eiraku, M.
*Combining Turing and 3D vertex models reproduces autonomous multicellular morphogenesis with
undulation, tubulation, and branching.* **Scientific Reports** 8, 2386 (2018).
[doi:10.1038/s41598-018-20678-6](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-018-20678-6).
